text: Receivables system options are the single most important setup record you'll touch before anything else works. There's one set per business unit, and almost every other piece of setup either reads a default from it or gets validated against it.

A business unit is the operating entity that processes transactions, and each one gets exactly one system options record. System options are grouped by category: accounting, which holds the AutoAccounting rule set and the ledger; cash processing, which covers unapplied and unidentified receipt accounts; transactions and customers, which covers site requirements and AutoInvoice error handling; and tax defaults. Three business units means three separate system options records.

Here's how AutoAccounting actually works. It's a rule engine that builds a GL account segment by segment, and for each segment you pick a source. In this example, the Revenue segment's natural account comes from the transaction type, and the cost center comes from the salesperson's territory. Every invoice entered with that transaction type and salesperson automatically gets the same revenue account, with nobody typing in a GL string by hand.

Picture Northwind Fixtures Co, with one business unit called Northwind US. Its system options point AutoAccounting's revenue segment at transaction type, and its unapplied-receipts account at a single suspense account. A rep enters a Standard Invoice, and AutoAccounting derives the full revenue account without anyone touching the chart of accounts directly.
